DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.899.setting: Six community mental health teams (9 general adult consultants), east side of North Wales (Wrexham and Flintshire), BETSI Health Board
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.899.standard: NICE ADHD guidance (adapted ADHD audit support tool)

cycle1.result: Good compliance with NICE guidance for assessment and treatment and in documenting diagnostic criteria (DSM-IV and/or ICD-10); deficiencies in recommended physical examination and side-effect monitoring; antipsychotics used in some patients. No numbers reported.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.899.other_findings: Case notes of 20 patients per consultant were audited. Recommendations included clinician education, local ADHD clinics and joining the POMH-UK ADHD prescribing QIP.

DOI:10.1177/2051415818792448.topic: Radical cystectomy practice and case volume
DOI:10.1177/2051415818792448.setting: British Association of Urological Surgeons audit and data platform; 84 centres, 161 surgeons in England

cycle1.result: Ileal conduit 85.2%; open cystectomy 67.8%, robotic 20.6%, laparoscopic 9.1%; lymph node dissection rates 79.5% to 90.3%; median LOS 7–9 days minimally invasive vs 11–12 days open.

DOI:10.1177/2051415818792448.other_findings: Robotic cystectomy was more likely in high-volume surgeons and centres; transfusion rates trended higher as centre volume fell; high-grade complications appeared under-reported.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.280.setting: Four general adult acute psychiatric wards, Aneurin Bevan Health Board
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.280.standard: Smoking status asked on admission and cessation advice or nicotine replacement therapy offered (target not reported)

cycle1.result: Smoking status asked in 68%; not asked n = 11 (32%); smoker not given advice n = 13 (38%); smoker given advice n = 4 (12%); advice or NRT given to only 14% of potential smokers.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.280.other_findings: Asking about smoking varied between wards and there was a lack of smoking cessation literature on the wards.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljad113.070.setting: Dermatology department, Barts Health NHS Trust, London
DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljad113.070.standard: British Association of Dermatologists 2020 guidelines: TB screening questions, chest X-ray and IGRA before biologics

cycle1.result: CXR performed in 74 (96%); IGRA in 72 (94%); 3 (4%) had latent TB on positive IGRA with normal CXR; no IGRA-negative patient had a positive CXR.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljad113.070.other_findings: Authors propose CXR only for patients symptomatic for TB or with a positive IGRA.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2025-003421.topic: Implementation of perinatal audit improvement objectives
DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2025-003421.setting: All 11 perinatal cooperation groups in the northern region of the Netherlands

cycle1.result: Knowledge and skills scores rose from mean 2.53 to 3.70 on a 1–5 Likert scale (p<0.001); 98 improvement objectives addressed, 46 (47%) fully implemented and secured.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2025-003421.intervention: ACTion method: 7-step PDCA cycle with interactive learning, training and coaching in implementation and behaviour change
DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2025-003421.other_findings: 86% of 93 team members completed training; implementation per team ranged from 14% to 67%. Barriers were limited time, manpower and commitment.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.224.standard: Public Health England national COVID-19 guidance

cycle1.result: SARS-CoV-2 detected in 1 patient; practice consistent with national guidance.

cycle2.dates: Third cycle, later wave of COVID-19, 2020
cycle2.result: SARS-CoV-2 detected in 12 patients; identification of suspected cases and management of confirmed cases consistent with national guidance.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.224.other_findings: Three cycles, one per wave; cycle 2 had 12 patients. All patients recovered; three needed oral antibiotics and dexamethasone and one was admitted to a general hospital for oxygen.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.638.topic: Physical health appointment attendance in psychiatric inpatients

cycle1.result: Attendance 68.5% of 89 appointments; missed rate 25.8%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.638.intervention: Measures addressing patient transfers, leave protocols and transport problems

cycle2.result: Attendance 71.8% of 39 appointments; missed rate 28.2%; chi-square 2.2893, p = 0.3183 (not significant).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.638.other_findings: Missed appointments in phase 2 were due to patient leave, ward cancellations and transport problems.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11750.setting: Stanley Treatment and Intervention Team, community mental health, Derwent Clinic
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11750.standard: General Medical Council professional standards for prescribing unlicensed medicines

cycle1.result: 2/27 initiated on unlicensed medication; both (2/2) had documented discussion, rationale, risk-benefit, accurate records and information given; 100% compliant.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11750.other_findings: Better than a previous inpatient ward audit. A set proforma for unlicensed prescribing was suggested.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.075.setting: Large teaching hospital, Kellgren Centre for Rheumatology, Manchester Royal Infirmary
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.075.standard: GIRFT guidance on broad MDT input (rheumatology, haematology, infectious diseases, critical care) and local HLH guidelines

cycle1.result: MDT discussion in 26/34; 1/26 (4%) met guideline standards; 13/26 (50%) single-specialty discussions; median 10 days admission to MDT, 19/26 (73%) within 14 days.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.075.other_findings: Mortality 6/26 (23%) with MDT discussion vs 5/8 (63%) without; organ support 14/26 (54%) vs 5/8 (63%). Overall mortality 11/34 (32%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.459.setting: Community mental health team, Glasgow, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.459.standard: NICE: weight, blood pressure and heart rate monitored every 6 months on ADHD medication

cycle1.result: Weight recorded 15%, heart rate 8%, blood pressure 19%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.459.intervention: Results presented at a local meeting with relevant clinicians in May 2021

cycle2.result: Weight recorded 45%, heart rate 40%, blood pressure 50%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.459.other_findings: 30 patients identified, 10 excluded for non-engagement. Still not meeting NICE guidance; COVID-19 reduced face-to-face reviews.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.586.setting: Wards 6 and 7 (old age psychiatry), Harplands Hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.586.standard: Trust NEWS2 standards, SOP 1.62a and Physical Health policy

cycle1.result: 37/39 charts completed at admission; 9 lacked demographics, 13 missing date/time, 6 missing signatures, 9 illegible entries, 12 incomplete sections; GCS issues in 2 charts.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.586.intervention: Printed patient information labels, targeted education sessions for ward teams and discussion with ward management
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.586.other_findings: Scores 1–4 were often escalated to a registered nurse first and scores >4 directly to medics; electronic versions of charts were often left unfilled. Re-audit planned.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.634.setting: Six wards (three geriatric, two medical, one surgical), district general hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.634.standard: Local mental health trust rapid tranquillisation guidance

cycle1.result: 13/297 (4.3%) received RT; indication documented in 50%; maximum frequency not indicated; no psychiatric liaison or dementia team involvement evident; post-RT monitoring not evident.

cycle2.result: 9/172 (5.2%) received RT; indication documented in 88.8%; maximum frequency indicated in 55.5%; almost 100% documentation of RT administration; liaison or dementia team involvement around 33%; post-sedation monitoring still not evident.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.634.other_findings: PRN and intramuscular remained most common. A new RT policy with teaching and training has since been approved, with re-audit planned in 6–12 months.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.261.setting: Trent Oesophago-Gastric Unit, Nottingham University Hospitals (high-volume UGI cancer unit)
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.261.standard: NICE: PET-CT for all oesophageal and OGJ cancers except T1a

cycle1.result: Mean wait for PET-CT 17 (1–57) days; 14 (32%) had CT/PET-CT discrepancy; 5 (11%) distant metastasis on PET-CT; 9 (20%) incidental uptake; further investigations added mean 15 (1–28) days delay.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.261.other_findings: Authors recommend timely PET-CT scanning and reporting, e.g. during pre-MDT triage.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.568.standard: NICE NG97 (1.5): consider memantine with acetylcholinesterase inhibitor in moderate to severe Alzheimer's dementia; Trust guidelines

cycle1.result: Severity documented in only 7% (all moderate), 93% generic diagnosis; 46/60 on medication, all on monotherapy; 46 completed the diagnostic pathway.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.568.other_findings: Mixed dementia 40%, Alzheimer's 39%, Lewy body 8% of diagnoses. Combination therapy not yet considered at diagnosis.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.06.setting: Frailty admission unit, Mid Yorkshire Hospitals NHS Trust (large district general)
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.06.standard: NICE CG103 and SIGN 157: delirium diagnosis with CAM or 4AT and management with care plan

cycle1.result: CAM or 4AT used in 32.5%; delirium care plan in 20%.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.06.intervention: Delirium care checklist sticker, brief education sessions for ward doctors and reminder emails over 6 weeks

cycle2.result: Sticker use fell from 57% in week 1 to 0% in week 6; 4AT 57%, 50%, 100% in first 3 weeks then 40%, 4.2%, 1.3%; care plan 42% and 37% in first 2 weeks, 0% by week 6.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afab030.06.other_findings: Barriers were lapse of education sessions due to registrar on-calls, junior doctor changeover, time to complete and unclear ownership between medical and nursing teams.

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2024.10.004.topic: COVID-19 infection and mortality after surgery
DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2024.10.004.setting: 43 centres in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland (multicentre national audit)

cycle1.result: COVID-19 in 0.52% (n=35); overall 30-day mortality 0.41%; mortality 25.71% (n=9) with COVID-19; adjusted OR 11.71 (95% CI 1.55 to 88.74, p=0.017).

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2024.10.004.other_findings: Mortality 75% (n=3) in diabetic foot surgery patients with COVID-19; post-lockdown infection rate 0.15% with no COVID deaths; complications and infection rates unchanged.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11844.setting: 15 memory services, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11844.standard: National benchmark of diagnosis within six weeks (42 days) of referral; National Audit of Dementia

cycle1.result: Access times 30–207 days, diagnostic waits 3–147 days, overall waits 92–323 days; no service met the six-week benchmark; 25% of services diagnosed within 6–18 weeks, 75% within 18–52 weeks.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11844.other_findings: Trust average waits exceeded national averages; the best service was at 92 days.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10540.topic: STOMP/STAMP psychotropic prescribing and physical health monitoring
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10540.setting: Leeds Community Healthcare Learning Disability Clinic (children and young people)

cycle1.result: Annual health check 70%; drug names and doses 100%; indication 85%; side-effect discussion at initiation 73%; side-effect enquiry at follow-up 77%.

cycle2.result: Annual health check 80%; drug names and doses 100%; indication 93%; side-effect discussion at initiation 38%; side-effect enquiry at follow-up 54%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10540.other_findings: Criteria were changed in cycle 2 (follow-up definition and age >14 for health checks), which may explain differences. Side-effect discussion was often missing for melatonin or ADHD medication.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11805.topic: Physical health equipment on psychiatric wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11805.setting: Seven inpatient wards (acute adult, older adult, forensic), The Redwoods Centre, Midlands Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11805.standard: RCPsych Physical Health in Mental Health (2009) equipment checklist; compliance standard 100%

cycle1.result: All wards >80% compliant; overall compliance 87%; neurological testing pins absent on most wards; alcometers, Snellen charts, ophthalmoscopes and otoscopes borrowed between wards.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11805.intervention: Formal equipment-sharing arrangements confirmed and procurement of missing equipment planned
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11805.other_findings: Re-audit planned 6 months after the first cycle.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11425.setting: Specialist community rehabilitation team, Sheffield Health Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11425.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists standards for community rehabilitation services

cycle1.result: Only 3/50 (6%) service users had formally recorded carers; survey response 24% (14/58); 93% had emergency contact information, 78% felt supported, 64% felt involved, 50% aware of carers groups, 14% given written information.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11425.intervention: Bimonthly family, friends and carers support group set up, written carers pack reviewed and definition of carer broadened
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11425.other_findings: All 14 respondents identified as carers, suggesting significant under-recording; EPR limits formal recording of carer status.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.449.setting: Three psychiatric units across three sites, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.449.standard: RCPsych and PRSB recommendations for letters to GPs

cycle1.result: Missing care coordinator details 91.7%, medical comorbidities 61.22%, non-psychiatric diagnosis 79.59%, actions for GP 71.43%; psychiatric diagnosis 83.47%, psychiatric medications and follow-up plan 80.17%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.449.intervention: Local guidelines and letter template with recommended headings, and formal teaching for junior doctors

cycle2.result: Psychiatric diagnosis 97.1% (previously 83.5%), psychiatric medication 91.4% (80.17%), follow-up plan 98.6% (80.2%); medical comorbidity 28.6% vs 31.4%, non-psychiatric medication 65.7% vs 34.7%, care coordinator 54.3% vs 8.3%, action for GP 27.1% vs 44.6%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.449.other_findings: Two headings declined and change varied between sites. Barriers were template not used, lack of junior training and psychiatrist workload.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10553.setting: Psychiatry clinics, TEWV NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10553.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists guidance on GP letters (January 2021), 10 domains

cycle1.dates: Letters September to December 2023; audited December 2023 to January 2024
cycle1.result: 100% for contact details, review date, consultation, participants and plan; venue and diagnosis 97%; medications 93%; care coordinator 60%; MSE 70%; risk 50%; user-friendly information 23%; allergies 13%; service users copied in 3%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10553.intervention: Updated GP letter template with sections for allergies, risk, user-friendly information and copying patients; dissemination via huddles, trainee handovers, laminated copies and email

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.7.002.setting: Major trauma centre, Cambridge University Hospitals

cycle1.result: BOAST compliance result not reported; FUSION vs ORIF showed no significant difference in EQ-5D-5L (P = 0.13), FAAM-ADL (P = 0.20), FAAM-Sport (P = 0.34), infection (P = 0.55), surgical time (P = 0.91) or time to weight bearing (P = 0.39).

DOI:10.1302/1358-992x.2023.7.002.other_findings: 15 open talus fractures in 14 patients: 7 ORIF, 5 fusion; mean follow-up four years and one month.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.229.topic: Antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring in learning disability
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.229.setting: CAMHS services, Surrey (children and young people with learning disability)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.229.standard: NICE guidelines on antipsychotic prescribing (tool based on an RCPsych audit)

cycle1.result: 5 prescribed antipsychotics, all with documented reason for starting; for 4 started more than 12 months ago, side effects, EPSE, weight, BP, glycaemic control and lipids not documented; 1 had no review in 6 months; 3 reviews did not consider dose reduction or stopping.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.229.other_findings: One patient transferred to primary care with clear transfer of prescribing responsibility and written guidance.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.467.topic: COVID-19 vaccination offer and uptake in inpatients
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.467.setting: Acute adult psychiatric wards (male, female, PICU), Highbury Hospital, Nottingham
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.467.standard: Trust policy: all eligible patients offered COVID-19 vaccine

cycle1.result: 105 (31%) vaccinated or planned before admission; 100/234 (43%) offered; 59% (n = 59) accepted; 92% (n = 55) of acceptors received vaccine.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.467.other_findings: Sectioned patients and those in psychotic clusters more often refused; acceptance 59% was below national 80%. Offering in rounds may have missed patients.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.458.standard: Trust seclusion policy in line with Mental Health Act Code of Practice 2015: 1-hour and 4-hourly medical reviews, MDT within 12 hours, documented review content

cycle1.result: Reviewed within 1 hour 34%; 4-hourly 41%; internal MDT 47%; review documented 57%; ongoing concerns 50%; MSE 47%; physical health 42%; medication 44%; risk 44%; need for seclusion 58%; intervention 52%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.458.other_findings: 107 seclusion episodes in 61 patients; the seclusion review template was poorly used by medics.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.310.standard: Mental Health Commission Judgment Support Framework version 5; target 100% physical examination on admission

cycle1.result: 3/13 had physical examination on admission (23% compliance); 6 had examination in ED before admission.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.310.intervention: Results presented to MDT and NCHDs; colour-coded physical examination proforma developed and briefed to all staff

cycle2.result: 7 examined on admission, 2 refusals documented; 100% compliance (examination done or reason documented).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.310.other_findings: Proforma to be audited every 6 months.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.441.topic: Admission blood tests in psychiatric inpatients
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.441.setting: Psychiatric intensive care unit, KMPT trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.441.standard: RCPsych Standards for Inpatient Mental Health Services: bloods within 24 hours of admission; standardised PICU blood panel

cycle1.result: 30% bloods within 24 hours, 10% on previous ward, 40% declined/unsafe, 20% not done in timeframe; 69% of direct admissions had all relevant tests, 23% some.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.441.intervention: Standardised PICU guideline with pre-filled blood test request form

cycle2.result: Only 6% not done within 24 hours; all consenting direct admissions (89%) had all standardised tests; conclusion reports 77% to 100% for full tests and 80% to 94% within 24 hours.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.441.other_findings: Completion remained lower for patients transferred from other wards. Plan to roll out pre-filled forms across all trust wards.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.623.setting: Alcohol service, Lorraine Hewitt House drug and addiction service
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.623.standard: NICE recommendation for fibroscanning (target not reported)

cycle1.result: 37% normal; 16% liver stiffness >10kPa, 15 referred to liver clinic; steatosis stage 1 13%, stage 2 18%, stage 3 29%; 10/15 (66.7%) attended liver clinic.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.623.other_findings: Scans covered about one third of clients with alcohol as primary substance; all had results discussed with lifestyle advice.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.431.setting: Low secure services unit, Northern England, South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.431.standard: Trust standards for completion of the Formulation Information Risk Management (FIRM) assessment

cycle1.result: Current/historical risks 100%; formulation 89%; Staying Safe/Staying Well care plan 73%; service user involved 16%; updated since last CPA 70%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.431.intervention: Findings presented at local academic meeting and distributed to staff
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.431.other_findings: Formulation and care plan completion improved compared with earlier auditing in October 2021 (figures not reported). Patient involvement was low, often because FIRM was completed at night.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10663.setting: Four old age psychiatry wards, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board, South Wales
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10663.standard: All-Wales DNACPR policy for adults (2015, revised 2024)

cycle1.result: Decision date missing in 2 forms; not signed with date and time in 1; not documented in clinical notes in 10; discussion with patient in 9; discussion with IMCA/attorney or family in 20; appropriate signatures in 17; 7 not countersigned in section 6.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10663.other_findings: Different versions of the DNACPR form were in use. Recommended a unified form and adding DNACPR and treatment escalation status to the ward round proforma.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.245.setting: Dublin North City and County CAMHS team
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.245.standard: Established ICP policy: every service user to have an individual care plan with key worker, formulation, goals, action plan, copy to family, review and discharge dates

cycle1.result: Overall ICP compliance 62%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.245.intervention: Findings and intervention discussed at multidisciplinary team meeting and wider CAMHS academic meeting

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.631.topic: GP referral quality to memory services
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.631.setting: Memory Clinic, South Sefton Neighbourhood Centre, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.631.standard: 100% completeness of referral information (green ≥95%, yellow 75–94%, red <75%)

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: History of memory loss 86%; duration of memory loss 46%; 8% reduction in documentation of impact on ADLs compared with 2019; about a quarter accepted on first referral; 70 inappropriate or declined.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.631.other_findings: 17 initially rejected referrals were accepted after GPs gave further details. A new referral proforma has since been designed with the local ICB.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaf142.287.setting: Oxted Health Centre, semi-rural general practice with 16,300 patients
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaf142.287.standard: NICE guidance on anti-resorptive or anabolic treatment after osteoporotic fragility fracture

cycle1.result: 51% not on any fracture prevention medication (reasons explained in 40%); 39% taking bisphosphonates; 10% prescribed but not taking oral bisphosphonates.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaf142.287.intervention: Dedicated clinics (telephone or face to face) to discuss management and start medication

cycle2.result: 49% started on medication; 9% refused; 17% deemed inappropriate; 25% had died or left the practice.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaf142.287.other_findings: Only direct consultation led to discussion and treatment.

cycle1.result: Unit mean error rate 12.5%.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.42.intervention: Automated Excel spreadsheet producing individual prescriber feedback forms, plus posters and discussion at clinical governance meetings

cycle2.result: Unit mean error rate 13.0%; in 7 prescribers with at least 5 items in both cycles, mean error rate fell from 15.3 (SD 14.6) to 9.4 (SD 7.3), p=0.29.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.42.other_findings: Limited by few data per prescriber and variable prescribing volume.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.331.setting: CMHT Inverness Sector A outpatient service, NHS Highland
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.331.standard: First appointment within 12 weeks of referral

cycle1.result: 140 (87.5%) given an appointment; mean wait 12 weeks for 103 (64%); 57 (36%) waited longer than 13 weeks; 20 (12.5%) referrals inadequate.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.331.other_findings: Delays due to DNAs, cancellations and postponement awaiting information. Plans to flag the 12-week deadline in a database and improve referral information.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.425.setting: Somerset NHS Foundation Trust (Severn Deanery), psychiatry placements
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.425.standard: Severn Deanery and Trust recommendation of one hour of supervision per week for psychiatry trainees

cycle1.result: Response rate 63%; 17% met supervisor only sometimes; WPBAs completed 89%; QI/audit discussed 66%; psychotherapy competencies partly discussed 42%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.425.intervention: Results highlighted in local teaching and audit meetings

cycle2.result: 9/27 responded (33%); 11% met supervisor only sometimes; WPBAs 88%; QI/audit discussed 60%; psychotherapy competencies discussed 75%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.425.other_findings: Most trainees were satisfied, but supervision needed protecting from clinical work.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.267.setting: Ward 3 old age psychiatry inpatient ward, Wishaw General Hospital, NHS Lanarkshire
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.267.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists standards for ward rounds

cycle1.result: No up-to-date MDT checklist information; 10% individual food and fluid charts; 0% in folders.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.267.intervention: Structured MDT ward round checklist developed through PDSA cycles, and food, fluid and weight charts kept in separate folders

cycle2.result: 44% up-to-date MDT checklist items; 100% food and fluid charts in folders.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.267.other_findings: November 2021 showed a 73% increase in up-to-date checklist items; the January fall was attributed to Omicron staff sickness.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2018-000490.setting: Three hospitals contributing to the Australian and New Zealand Hip Fracture Registry

cycle1.result: Overall data agreement 82.3%; data completeness 95.6%.

DOI:10.1136/bmjoq-2018-000490.other_findings: Half of disagreements were information discrepancies, a quarter missing data and a quarter time/date/number; transcription caused 1 in 50. A generic data quality audit framework is proposed.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.175.setting: Department of general surgery, Wrightington, Wigan and Leigh NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.175.standard: NICE and Good Medical Practice: written and verbal information for people with pancreatitis and families

cycle1.result: 60% not satisfied with information; none given written information; more than 90% not shown a diagram; not informed about investigations 40%, treatment 60%, verbal information 26%, alcohol as cause 27%.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.175.intervention: Results shared with surgical team and patient information leaflet designed and given to every patient

cycle2.result: Improvement in almost all areas; overall satisfaction improved from 60% to 92%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.295.setting: Inpatient adult intellectual disability assessment and treatment unit, NHS Highland
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.295.standard: NHS Highland Seclusion Policy: 15-minute monitoring, reviews at 2 and 4 hours, Datix on commencement

cycle1.result: Anxiolytic use before seclusion, respiration rate and appearance at 15-minute checks, plans to end seclusion at 2 hours and informing duty consultant at 4 hours often missing; Datix not always submitted. No figures reported.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.295.intervention: Results shared via Seclusion Policy Short Life Working Group, internal teaching, clinical governance forum and trainee induction; protocol drafts updated
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.295.other_findings: Commonest reason for seclusion was increasing agitation and aggression. Re-audit planned.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11359.standard: NICE: height, weight, blood pressure, heart rate with centiles and growth charts for children on ADHD medication

cycle1.result: Height and weight 97%; BP and HR 100%; height/weight centiles and growth charts 85%; BP centiles 10%; HR centiles 0%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11359.intervention: Results presented at local department meeting and posters of NICE guidelines distributed

cycle2.result: Height, weight, their centiles, HR, BP and growth charts 100%; BP centiles 2%; HR centiles 0%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11359.other_findings: The electronic record cannot convert BP and HR to centiles, limiting compliance.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10655.topic: Physical health equipment on psychiatric wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10655.setting: Four old age psychiatric wards, the Mount hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10655.standard: CQC physical health recommended equipment list and equipment needed for NICE antipsychotic monitoring

cycle1.result: not reported

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10655.intervention: Recommendations from the first audit (details not reported)

cycle2.result: No ward had all equipment; 17.5–35% of recommended items unavailable; alcometer, Snellen chart, BMI chart and tuning fork missing on all wards; expired blood bottles and urinalysis sticks; only otoscope and ophthalmoscope not working.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10655.other_findings: No significant improvement from the first cycle; variable ECG machine function means QT monitoring is unreliable.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10616.topic: Handover between emergency department and psychiatric wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10616.setting: 9 mental health inpatient wards across 3 locations in one trust

cycle1.result: 28 (62%) had no SBAR handover documented; 8 (28%) no discharge summary; 5 had neither; 25 (56%) returned with ward actions, 5 (20%) of which were delayed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10616.other_findings: Extension of an earlier single-ward audit, showing improvement on previous findings (figures not reported). All but one ward identified handover problems.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10600.topic: Delirium and dementia assessment in older inpatients
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10600.setting: Psychiatric liaison service, busy district general hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10600.standard: Local and national delirium and dementia guidelines (4AT, PINCH ME)

cycle1.result: 51.3% referred to Delirium and Dementia team; PINCH ME used by referring team in 28.2% and by liaison in 10.2%; antipsychotics in 30.7%; follow-up arranged in 82.1%; 35% referred to memory clinic.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10600.intervention: Educational initiatives and closer collaboration with the Delirium and Dementia team
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10600.other_findings: 43.6% had pre-existing dementia and 28.2% were admitted with acute confusion.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.415.setting: Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust (trust-wide)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.415.standard: CNTW seclusion policy: independent seclusion review must include an Approved Clinician

cycle1.result: Senior clinicians at ISR: 83% medical, 11% non-medical AC, 6% neither; 68% of medical clinicians not AC grade; 0% of non-AC medical ISRs documented discussion with an AC; 29% out of hours.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.415.intervention: Seclusion policy changed so ISRs must be done by an AC except in extreme circumstances, when discussed with an AC
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.415.other_findings: 96 of 260 seclusion episodes triggered an ISR; 72% of non-AC doctors were SHO grade.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac125.006.setting: Ten national hip fracture audits (international comparison)
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac125.006.standard: Fragility Fracture Network 2014 minimum common dataset (32 questions)

cycle1.result: 215 questions tabulated; 72 (34%) used in >1 audit, 32 (15%) by more than half; 21/32 (65%) MCD fields used by the majority; only three used by all ten audits.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac125.006.other_findings: A revised minimum common dataset was developed with international feedback.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10675.setting: Mental Health of Learning Disabilities team, Kent and Medway
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10675.standard: NICE guidance on ADHD medication monitoring in the past 6 months

cycle1.result: Weight measured in last 6 months 83%; pulse 76.5%; blood pressure 64%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10675.other_findings: 15% (N=97) of 629 MHLD patients had confirmed ADHD; 43% (N=42) of these were on medication, mostly methylphenidate (62%).

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead104.254.setting: Rheumatology department, South Eastern Health and Social Care Trust (Ulster Hospital)

cycle1.result: All had ESR and CRP; ANCA in 43 (3 positive); CT brain in 40; TA ultrasound once; CT-PET in 6; 70 TAB with 12 positive and 4 suggestive.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead104.254.intervention: Rapid access GCA pathway being designed
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/kead104.254.other_findings: Temporal artery ultrasound and CT-PET were under-used.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.414.topic: Eating disorder assessment and risk monitoring
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.414.setting: Tier 3 community CAMHS, South Lanarkshire, NHS Lanarkshire

cycle1.result: Recording: weight change 40%, hydration 40%, temperature 5%, over-exercising 85%, purging 75%, self-harm 85%, BP/HR 80%, ECG 75%, engagement 75%.

cycle2.result: Weight change 80%, hydration 70%, temperature 30%, over-exercising 90%, purging 85%, self-harm 90%, BP/HR 50%, ECG 40%, engagement 60%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.414.other_findings: Mean time to initial assessment 63 days (40% within 4 weeks); 15% received no intervention. Standard remains inadequate.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.597.topic: STOMP/STAMP psychotropic prescribing and physical health monitoring
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.597.setting: Alders Warrington CAMHS, Mersey Care NHS
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.597.standard: RCPsych Position Statement PS05/21 (STOMP) and Mersey Care Consent to Examination and Treatment Policy SD06; 14 compliance standards

cycle1.result: Overall STOMP compliance 98% (significant assurance); indication documented for all; 1 (6%) had no behavioural support plan before medication; all had MDT before prescribing, 3-monthly reviews, specialist prescriber and capacity documented.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.597.other_findings: Three criteria were not met. 3 (17%) had medication indicated for behavioural problems.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11821.topic: Time to first appointment after referral
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11821.setting: Older People's Service CMHT, North Leeds, LYPFT
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11821.standard: LYPFT guidance: seen within 15 working days of referral (trust standard 80%); electronic documentation within 24 hours; GP letter within 2 weeks

cycle1.result: 70% seen within 15 working days; reason for delay documented 33%; electronic documentation 100%, within 24 hours 73%; GP letter sent 87%, within 2 weeks 33%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11821.intervention: Resident doctors added to gatekeeping assessment rota; reminders to document reasons for delay; record of patients not accepted with admin reminders to complete GP letters within 2 weeks

cycle2.result: 87% seen within 15 working days; reason for delay documented 40%; electronic documentation 97%, within 24 hours 61%; GP letter sent 79%, within 2 weeks 41%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11821.other_findings: Referrals rose from 80 to 100. Documentation timeliness gave mixed results under greater service pressure.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znaf036.007.topic: Braun procedure for bile reflux after OAGB

cycle1.result: 35/1024 (3.4%) OAGB patients needed surgery for bile reflux; 31 had Braun procedure, 27/31 (88%) immediate resolution and 23 (74%) at 2 years; 4/31 (13%) failed and converted to RYGB.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znaf036.007.other_findings: All 8 RYGB conversions had resolution at 1 year; Braun was a day case vs 2-day stay for RYGB.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.645.topic: Methadone dosing in opioid substitution therapy
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.645.standard: Clinical guidance of therapeutic methadone dose 60–120mg; documented reason for sub-therapeutic dosing and evidence of instability

cycle1.result: 54% undergoing dose change; 46% maintained below 60mg (8 declined advised change, 15 no advice recorded); of 8 using illicit opioids, 63% advised increase but declined and 25% not advised; of 21 using other substances, 48% had no OST change considered.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.645.other_findings: 285 patients were on <60mg. Recommendations were further training and at least 6-monthly strategic care plan reviews.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11753.setting: Chesterfield Mental Health Liaison Team, acute hospital, Derbyshire Healthcare Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11753.standard: 100% documentation of capacity assessment; minimum Grade 2 detail for all four functional stages

cycle1.result: Broad capacity assessment recorded in 90%; specific decision documented in 37%; no evidence (Grade 0) for Understanding and Communicating in 50%, and for Weighing-up in 40%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11753.intervention: Recommended mandatory MCA forms in the core electronic assessment template

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.541.setting: Rathbone Rehabilitation Centre, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Smoking status recorded 47 (92%); 26/28 (93%) smokers offered support on admission; 24/31 (77%) offered support at regular intervals; 20/28 (71%) offered NRT; 5/31 referred to Nicotine Dependence Treatment Advisor.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.541.intervention: Action plan: reminders via team meetings and emails, completion of physical health nursing proforma, and posters on the referral pathway

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.332.topic: Handover information on transfer to emergency department
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.332.setting: Peter Bruff Mental Health Assessment Unit and Ardleigh Acute Inpatient Ward, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.332.standard: PRSB Ambulance handover to emergency care standard V1.0: 100% of transfers with a doctor's support letter

cycle1.result: Peter Bruff: support letter in 1 of 6 transfers (17%); Ardleigh: 2 of 5 (40%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.332.intervention: Template care summary and handover letter created

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.244.setting: Rheumatology department, Glasgow Royal Infirmary, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde

cycle1.result: 30.89% lacked examination findings; 69.10% no further investigations documented beyond haematological/radiological; 53.65% had no differential diagnosis documented.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.244.other_findings: 38.2% requested advice, 60.16% review and 1.63% takeover; ongoing education for resident doctors recommended.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11735.setting: Acute old age psychiatry inpatient wards, Royal Edinburgh Hospital, NHS Lothian
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11735.standard: All inpatient deaths reported via DATIX

cycle1.result: 7/14 deaths reported on DATIX (all 3 unexpected, 4 expected); 50% not reported.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11735.intervention: MCCD issuing made electronic and senior management informed all teams of the need to report every death
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11735.other_findings: Expected deaths in particular were not reported consistently.

DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2014-307263.422.topic: Coeliac testing in irritable bowel syndrome
DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2014-307263.422.setting: St Johns Surgery, large semi-rural general practice (11,250 patients), Bromsgrove
DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2014-307263.422.standard: NICE guidance: test for coeliac disease in patients with IBS symptoms

cycle1.result: 65/250 tested for coeliac disease; 185 not tested.

DOI:10.1136/gutjnl-2014-307263.422.other_findings: No significant difference in poverty or depression between tested and untested patients; 137 untested had no further investigations.
